summary: Dedicated throughput fingerprint shift caused by background health-scan impacting autoscale behavior
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sustained 30-50% drop in dedicated-pool throughput for their reserved capacity window starting 2026-03-10 10:40 UTC. The drop correlates with elevated attach latency and increased prefetch retries. Impact: multiple production jobs saw increased tail latency and several 504s to the customer-facing service.

Impact:
- Customer-visible p95 token latency increased from ~220ms to ~620ms.
- Throughput for pinned route fell by ~45% for a 90 minute window.
- Some requests returned 504/timeout during autoscaler attach backoff.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool (tenant: veridian-prod-dedicated).
- Region: us-east-1.
- Model routing: pinned rwd-llama2-13b-q4 primary, fallback to open-7b-q8_0.

Steps to reproduce / Observed sequence:
1) 10:38 UTC: periodic background "health-scan" job (snapshot integrity + weight-validate) started on several nodes in the reserved pool (operator-initiated maintenance).
2) 10:40-10:45 UTC: allocator attach latencies rose (logs show 500ms -> 1.8s attach handshake delays).
3) Autoscaler observed rising attach latency and classified capacity as constrained -> increased scale-up attempts and then triggered conservative cooldowns.
4) Prefetcher started thrashing KV cache entries due to snapshot read IO causing NVMe contention on two GPUs; this produced noisy-neighbor symptoms (per-node IO wait spikes).
5) 10:45-12:15 UTC: sustained throughput loss (~45%) with intermittent request timeouts.

Relevant logs and traces referenced below.

Observed behaviour vs expected:
- Expected: background maintenance runs to be IO-throttled and not reduce tenant throughput below SLA.
- Observed: maintenance caused elevated host IO wait leading to attach timeouts and autoscaler misclassification, which in turn reduced throughput and increased request errors.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Support temporarily disabled the non-critical health-scan on the affected nodes at 11:05 UTC (operator rollback).
- We moved the tenant traffic to a warm spare GPU stripe at 11:12 UTC (manual routing) which gradually restored throughput.
- Customer was notified and put on high-touch status.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:07 - Support (Aisha Khan): Confirmed with SRE that health-scan was scheduled and running on two reserved nodes. We recommended pausing the job and monitoring attach latencies.
2026-03-10 11:20 - SRE (Daniel Park): Paused health-scan across affected nodes. Noted NVMe io_wait spikes in node metrics (node-ue1-d-14, node-ue1-d-18). Initiating node-level io diagnostics.
2026-03-10 11:35 - Customer (Veridian SRE - Priya Rao): Noticed token p95 coming down slowly after re-routing. Appreciate quick response. Please advise whether this will reoccur.
2026-03-10 12:05 - Support (Marta Lopez): We are keeping the node scans off for now. Next step: patch prefetcher to back off under elevated nvme_io_wait; scheduling with infra team. ETA 2026-03-12.

2026-03-11 09:15 - SRE (Daniel Park): Root-cause hypothesis: background health-scan read pattern created large sequential NVMe bandwidth that competed with prefetcher small-random IO, causing NVMe scheduler starvation and elevated GPU attach times. Working on a limiting PR.

2026-03-12 14:02 - Engineering (Samir Patel): Submitted PR to add IO throttling and health-scan niceness: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4789. Patch includes prefetcher backoff threshold tied to node io_wait metric.
2026-03-12 16:45 - Support (Marta Lopez): Notified customer of planned fix and scheduled controlled rollout to canary nodes on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.
investigation_notes: Examined allocator traces: multiple attach attempts per request increased attach handshake retries from avg 1.1 to 3.6 during peak window.
NVMe io_wait correlated with prefetcher eviction spikes measured via metrics.prefetch.evictions which spiked 6x.
Autoscaler telemetry showed a decision boundary flip: attach_latency > 800ms -> treat as scarcity and throttle new routing. This threshold triggered conservative behaviour during noisy IO.
Node-level dmesg contained repeated nvme timeouts on node-ue1-d-14 during window (investigating firmware counters).
Prefetcher currently lacks backpressure when underlying storage signals sustained io_wait. Hypothesis: add reactive backoff to prefetcher and schedule health-scan with IO cgroup limits.
Looked at tenant traffic patterns: Veridian has many parallel short streams that are sensitive to attach latency. This amplified noisy-neighbor impact compared to long-batch tenants.
resolution_summary: Temporary and permanent mitigations: (1) Immediately paused health-scan and re-routed tenant to warm-stripe to restore throughput. (2) Engineering delivered PR to rate-limit health-scan IO and add prefetcher backoff tied to node io_wait metrics (PR #4789). (3) Canary rollout scheduled for 2026-03-13; full rollout after 24h canary with monitoring. (4) Recommended changes to runbooks: schedule heavy maintenance jobs outside reserved windows or use IO-cgroup throttling.
